grade.summary: The submitted proof is complete and correct. The lexicographically decreasing pair consisting of the total prime-exponent sum and the number of entries greater than 1 proves termination. The proof also establishes that every move leaves at least one entry greater than 1. Finally, the gcd of the valuation tuple for each prime is invariant under the Euclidean-algorithm transformation, and at termination these invariants uniquely determine M.
strengths: The total exponent sum is finite and strictly decreases whenever the selected integers have nontrivial gcd.
When the selected integers are coprime, the exponent sum is unchanged but the number of entries greater than 1 decreases, giving valid lexicographic descent.
The argument that the two replacement values cannot both equal 1 ensures that a terminal board contains exactly one entry greater than 1.
The primewise identity gcd(x,y)=gcd(min(x,y),|x-y|) is correctly justified, including zero and equal-exponent cases.
At a terminal board the invariant gcd of the p-adic valuations equals v_p(M), so all prime exponents of M depend only on the initial board.
